practiceReport.name: Amik Robertson
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (7th NFL season, 98% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday (veteran maintenance profile, awaiting Thursday workload)
practiceReport.beatComment: Robertson was unable to play against the Bengals on Monday due to an ankle injury that he picked up during Friday's practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a chance at playing against the Cardinals on Sunday.

practiceReport.name: Treylon Burks
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
practiceReport.beatComment: Burks presumably had his reps capped for maintenance purposes, as the wideout was sidelined for the Commanders' Week 9 loss to the Rams due to the same foot issue before suiting up in the ensuing two contests. In both of those games, Burks played north of 60 percent of the offensive snaps while producing a combined 4-57-0 receiving line on six targets. Provided he advances to full practice activity by Friday, Burks should head into this weekend's game in Arizona without a designation.

practiceReport.name: Jayden Daniels
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (94% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

practiceReport.name: Sonny Styles
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (93% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.

practiceReport.name: John Bates
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Bates went without a target for the fourth straight game. The 29-year-old's 21 offensive snaps ranked third at tight end behind Chig Okonkwo (49) and Ben Sinnott (24), and Bates should continue to have no fantasy value in Week 12 versus the Cardinals.

practiceReport.name: Andrew Wylie
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (G) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).

practiceReport.name: Rachaad White
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (RB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.

practiceReport.name: Colson Yankoff
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

practiceReport.name: Stefon Diggs
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Diggs was away from the team for Wednesday's session due to a personal issue. There's no indication this will be a long-term absence, and the Commanders did excuse him for Wednesday. Still, Diggs' return to the team will be worth monitoring over the coming days in advance of Sunday's game at Arizona.

practiceReport.name: Quan Martin
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Dyami Brown
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Laremy Tunsil
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Javontae Jean-Baptiste
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 7 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Jean-Baptiste was already ruled out for Monday night's game against the 49ers due to a pectoral injury, which is severe enough for the third-year pro to go on IR. He's required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he is eligible to return is Week 11 against the Bengals on Monday, Nov. 23.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Daron Payne
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Payne will be out long-term with a foot injury suffered in practice. With both Javon Kinlaw (knee) and Payne out, Tim Settle will have a larger role at nose tackle going forward.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Javon Kinlaw
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Washington placed Kinlaw on injured reserve Tuesday, but it wasn't immediately known how much time the knee injury he initially sustained Week 6 would keep him out of commission. Now that Kinlaw has opted for surgery, he'll remain on IR for the Commanders' final 10 games in what amounts to another major hit to the defensive line. Washington also placed nose tackle Daron Payne on IR on Tuesday after he needed surgery to repair a Jones fracture in his left foot.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jaylin Lane
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Lane sustained his season-ending ankle injury during the Commanders' Week 4 win against the Colts, and the injury was severe enough for him to stay in London overnight to be monitored and undergo additional tests. His absence has opened the door to more playing time for both Luke McCaffrey and Dyami Brown, and they are both candidates for another bump in playing time after Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jeremy McNichols
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Leo Chenal
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Chenal's move to injured reserve doesn't come as a surprise since it was previously announced he would undergo season-ending neck surgery. The 2022 third-round pick had racked up 18 tackles (nine solo) across three games before getting hurt and will now shift his focus to getting healthy for the 2027 campaign.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Terry McLaurin
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The surgery was conducted in New York, and McLaurin has already been ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. His availability for the start of the 2027 campaign will also be in question, as the veteran wideout faces a lengthy rehab process. The Commanders will move forward with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks atop the wideout depth chart this season.
